Variants.Content: Menetragos is located in the highlands of Norvos and the upper reaches of the Rhoyne River. Politically, it is within the hinterland under the rule of the city-state of Norvos and its bell. It is a town, a center where surrounding populations, markets, roads and local power converge. Walls and roads tied the surrounding population, storage, and garrison here; even if the flags were changed, this stronghold would still affect how nearby people paid taxes, traded, and sought refuge.

Entry Menetegos Local families also relied on mountain roads, bells, timber, river transportation, and farms protected by the city-state; if any road, well, or dock failed, the price would fall first on them.

Entry Menetegos Menetegos is located in the power and trade network of the Norvos Highlands, and the rules inside and outside the city gates are determined by the local order; whether the defenders are well fed and whether reinforcements can arrive on time are more important than the rhetoric in the council chamber in determining whether this stronghold is reliable.

Entry Menetegos They also recognize the accents, laws, and credentials of the Norvos Highlands; reputations can travel great distances from taverns, but true distances must still be measured by wheel, oar, or horse's hooves.

Entry Menetegos Menetegos is located in the power and trade network of the Norvos Highlands, and the rules inside and outside the city gates are determined by the local order; after the flag is changed, the roads, granaries, old debts, and local trusts still have to be taken over by the new owners one by one.

Entry Menetegos If you can supply supplies, avoid danger, and find a guide, it is worth marking in your itinerary; if you don't have these three things, no matter how loud your family name is, it won't be able to save the lost.

Craftsmen used their hands to measure Menetegos's workshops, markets, roof tiles, church bells and the streets that have expanded through the ages. Priests used rituals to continue the bearded monks, three bells and strict religious order. A stronghold was therefore not just a lord's hall, but also a place where weddings and funerals, vows, labor and local memories recurred.

Entry Menetegos They care about mountain roads, bells, timber, river transportation, and farms protected by the city-state. They also look at whether seeds are left after harvesting grain, and whether the city gates are open in times of disaster. When people from afar see coats of arms, what they see is whether there will be food to eat tomorrow.
